title: Proteome of neutrophils upon migration towards inflamed synovial fluid
projectDescription: Analysis of neutrophil proteomic alterations induced by migration towards inflamed joints in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). In this experiment neutrophil proteomes were investigated after migration towards JIA synovial fluid in an in vitro model of a synovial membrane, compared to neutrophils incubated in synovial fluid without migration. The migration model consisted of transwell inserts with human knee synoviocytes on the undersides and HMEC endothelial cells on the insides, placed in wells containing medium with 10 % JIA synovial fluid.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Healthy donor neutrophils were allowed to migrate towards JIA synovial fluid in an in vitro migration model of transwell inserts covered with primary human knee synoviocytes on the undersides and HMEC endothelial cells on the insides. Inserts were placed in wells containing media and 10 % JIA synovial fluid. Neutrophils were added to transwell inserts, or as migration controls to wells without inserts, and incubated for 1h at 37 °C. Synovial fluid from three patients were used and all conditions performed in triplicates. Neutrophils in wells were collected and purified based on CD66b-expression. Collected neutrophils were lysed in RIPA with protease inhibitors, and proteins precipitated in 90 % EtOH. Proteins were treated with dithioreitol (DTT) and iodoacetamide (IAA) and trypsinated. Peptides were analyzed by LC-MS on a fusion tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific), operated in the positive data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data was processed by Proteome Discoverer version 2.2 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and peptides were identified using SEQUEST HT against UniProtKB human database (release 2019-01-24).
